topic_title: Integration by Substitution With Inverse Trigonometric Functions

findings.observation: Hard question 4/(16x^2+4) reduces exactly to 1/(1+4x^2), an easy-form integrand. Raw non-unit coefficients do not reliably establish the hard label. Cancellation is valid; retain it with suitable calibration rather than forcing awkward coefficients.

All 8 easy and all 8 moderate questions have lower bound zero. All 8 hard questions have symmetric bounds. Every sine family uses normalized positive endpoint 1/2; every tangent family uses 1. This is a narrow authored progression, unlike the varied normalization/endpoint work in source hard examples.

Correct 2*pi/9 appears alongside zero, -2*pi/9, 2*pi/9+1 and 2*pi/9+2. Offset options are generic fallback choices, not clearly derived learner errors. Easy inverse-secant banks include a bare linear return-substitution distractor in 7 of 8 cases.
No imported hard questions in these two KPs. Hard bands are authored extrapolations; do not describe them as independently source-calibrated.
